newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Spain, Portugal determined to join EMU from start.
newsitem.headline: Spain, Portugal determined to join EMU from start.

text.p: Portugal and Spain are committed to joining the European Union's planned single currency from the start, the countries' leaders said on Saturday.
Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres, speaking just before a one-day European Union summit on Saturday, said, "I met the Spanish Prime Minister (Jose Maria Aznar) this weekend.
"It is a very strong commitment of both governments, both countries, to join a single European currency at the beginning."

Guterres said that his country would not be able to trim its overall debt to reach the EU's target ceiling of 60 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) in time to qualify for the first wave of entry to economic and monetary union (EMU).

But he said that heavily-indebted countries such as Belgium, widely viewed as certain to join the single currency on the January 1, 1999 launch date, would have to be included on the basis that its debt was declining fast enough to qualify.
"Some of the countries which will surely be with the founding members will not have the 60 percent of GDP debt (ratio) -- Belgium (for example)..." Guterres said.
"I cannot see a single currency without Belgium. If you want to include Belgium, you have to look at debt as a tendency, not as a fixed level."
Although Portugal would not meet the debt target in 1997, the crucial year for deciding which countries qualify for EMU, its debt would be declining as a proportion of GDP, he said.
Spain's Aznar told a news conference there had been a dramatic change of sentiment about Spain's prospects.
"Some months ago, there were doubts practically everywhere that Spain would be able to form part of the monetary union at the begining," he said.
"Now there are no doubts anywhere that Spain can and will be part of the monetary union at the beginning," he added.
Asked about reported differences between Spain and Italy over their strategy for joining EMU, he said:
"I want Italy to have the same success (as Spain) and be part of monetary union from the beginning."

One country widely regarded as likely to make the first wave of EMU is Finland and financial markets have been speculating that its markka currency will soon join the EU's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM), a system designed to help its currencies converge.
But Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Saturday he did not expect the EU summit to discuss any plans for the markka's entry to the ERM.
